'''''Festuca occidentalis''''' is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] known as '''western fescue'''. It is native to much of the northern half of [[North America]] and is most widely distributed in the west. It is most often found in forest and woodland habitat. The [[Botanical name#Components of plant names|specific epithet]] ''occidentalis'' is [[Latin]], meaning "western".

==Description==
''Festuca occidentalis'' is a tufted fescue that lacks [[rhizome]]s. The smooth and shiny [[Culm (botany)|culm]]s are {{convert|50-110|cm|abbr=on}} tall. Culms have two exposed nodes and have glabrous internodes. The shoots are intravaginal.

The leaf sheaths are glabrescent and rounded with a prominent midvein. The position of the [[Auricle (botany)|auricle]] is marked by a distinct swelling. The minutely erose [[ligule]] is {{convert|0.1-0.4|mm|abbr=on}} long. The basal leaves are capillary and {{convert|5-30|cm|abbr=on}} long. In cross section, the leaf blades are {{convert|0.25-0.5|mm|abbr=on}} wide and {{convert|0.3-0.65|mm|abbr=on}} thick, with three large veins and one to five ribs. The basal offshoots are erect, arising from the tops of the pale brown sheaths.

The lax, subsecund, flexuous [[panicle]] is {{convert|10-25|cm|abbr=on}} long. The panicle has two unequal and strongly reflexed branches at the lower node, with branches {{convert|1-5|cm|abbr=on}} long bearing minute trichomes. The three to five flowered [[spikelet]]s are {{convert|6-10|mm|abbr=on}} long. The [[Rachilla (floral axis)|rachilla]] is visible at anthesis and internodes are {{convert|1-1.5|mm|abbr=on}} long. The unequal [[glume]]s are narrow and acute. The lower glume is {{convert|2-3.6|mm|abbr=on}} long with one vein, and the upper glume is {{convert|3-3.4|mm|abbr=on}} long with one to two veins. The membranaceous, oblong to lanceolate [[Lemma (botany)|lemma]]s are {{convert|5-6.5|mm|abbr=on}} long, with slender, flexuous [[Awn (botany)|awn]]s {{convert|2.5-7|mm|abbr=on}} long. [[Palea (botany)|Palea]]s have inflexed sides that meet in the middle, measuring {{convert|4-5.5|mm|abbr=on}} long. Lodicules are toothed and lack trichomes. [[Anther]]s are {{convert|1-2|mm|abbr=on}} long. The [[Ovary (botany)|ovary]] is pubescent at its apex.<ref name=Manual>{{cite book |title=Gray's Manual of Botany |author=Merrit Lyndon Fernald |year=1970 |editor=R. C. Rollins |publisher=D. Van Nostrand Company |edition=Eighth (Centennial) - Illustrated|isbn=0-442-22250-5 |page=106}}</ref><ref name=Canada>{{cite book |page=[https://archive.org/details/fescuegrassesofc00aike/page/51 51] |title=Fescue grasses of Canada |url=https://archive.org/details/fescuegrassesofc00aike/page/51 |publisher=Canada Department of Agriculture |author=Aiken, S. G. |author2=Darbyshire, S. J. |name-list-style=amp |year=1935 |isbn=0-660-13483-7 }}</ref>

It flowers from late June into July.

==Distribution and habitat ==
''Festuca occidentalis'' occurs in the northern United States from the [[Bruce Peninsula]] to northern [[Michigan]] and eastern [[Wisconsin]], and from [[Montreal]] and [[British Columbia]] south to [[Wyoming]] and [[California]].<ref name=Manual/>

It grows in dry to moist woods, thickets, and rocky slopes. It grows up to {{convert|3100|m|abbr=on}} in elevation.<ref name=North>{{cite book |page=437 |title=Flora of North America: North of Mexico |volume=24 |author=Flora of North America Editorial Committee |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=1993 |isbn=9780195310719}}</ref>
